security_audit.summary: Most static matches are benign documentation syntax, schema URLs, or defensive credential guidance. Confirmed risks include remote pipe-to-shell commands, plaintext private-key storage guidance, executable installation into a home directory, and outbound network requests. Semantic review also identified unsafe delegation to mutable remote skills, unverified archive extraction, unrestricted URL probing, and coordinated engagement behavior.

remediation.issue: Documentation recommends piping remote scripts directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Require a pinned release, download the file separately, verify its checksum or signature, inspect it, and then execute it locally.

remediation.issue: The routing flow treats changing remote skills as authoritative instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist trusted sources, pin immutable revisions, verify signatures or hashes, and treat all loaded skill text as untrusted data.

remediation.issue: Credential guidance permits private keys and tokens in plaintext gitignored files.
remediation.suggestion: Use an operating system credential store or encrypted vault, restrict file permissions, and avoid storing verification codes unless required.

remediation.issue: The KodaClaw command extracts an unverified remote archive directly into an executable search path.
remediation.suggestion: Download a pinned archive, verify a published checksum or signature, inspect its contents, and install the expected binary explicitly.

remediation.issue: The status checker accepts unrestricted URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict schemes and destinations, reject loopback and private network addresses, disable redirects, and document that arbitrary URLs are unsafe.

remediation.issue: The playbook prescribes routine upvotes and mandatory replies as engagement tactics.
remediation.suggestion: Require user approval for social actions and limit engagement to relevant, authentic responses that follow each platform policy.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Remote Skills Treated as Authoritative
semantic_findings.description: The routing flow tells agents to fetch changing platform skills, treat them as authoritative, and follow them directly. Without pinning, integrity checks, or instruction isolation, a compromised remote skill can inject instructions and trigger unauthorized actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly calls remote skills authoritative, directs the agent to follow them, and recommends re-fetching changed versions. No verification or trust boundary is specified.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Remote Archive Installed as Executable
semantic_findings.description: The KodaClaw route streams a mutable release archive into tar and extracts it directly into ~/.local/bin. It provides no version pin, checksum, signature, or archive-content validation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The complete installation command is present and visibly lacks integrity verification. The destination is an executable search path.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted URL Probing
semantic_findings.description: The status checker accepts any URL and opens it without scheme or destination validation. Agent-supplied targets can reach loopback, private network, metadata, or redirected endpoints.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The positional URL is copied directly into the request path and urllib follows supported targets. No allowlist, address filtering, or redirect restriction is present.

semantic_findings.title: Coordinated Engagement Automation
semantic_findings.description: The skill prescribes replying to every comment and upvoting a fixed number of other posts each session. Automated execution can create inauthentic engagement or violate platform rules.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly define repeated posting, reply, and upvote behavior as obligations. The skill does not require operator approval or relevance checks for each social action.

content.value_statement: Agent community requirements, access methods, and status information are scattered across many platforms. This skill organizes platform routes, participation steps, status checks, and credential guidance.
actual_capabilities: Compares agent platforms by participation goal, availability, registration method, and verification requirement.
Routes users to platform-specific skills, interfaces, command-line tools, and API documentation.
Provides registration, posting, commenting, notification, and rate-limit guidance for listed communities.
Checks one supplied URL or all configured platform URLs and reports HTTP availability.
Explains credential storage, rotation, logging, and human verification practices.
Provides templates for project announcements, community replies, and notification maintenance.
limitations: Platform details and availability can become outdated after the listed September 2026 checks.
Several workflows require network access, external accounts, command-line tools, or human verification.
The skill does not validate the safety or authenticity of remote platform skills and installation artifacts.
The status checker reports HTTP reachability only and does not verify platform functionality.

use_cases.title: Choose a Community
use_cases.description: Compare communities by registration method, audience, availability, and verification needs before selecting a platform.

use_cases.title: Plan Community Operations
use_cases.description: Prepare posting, reply, notification, and rate-limit workflows across selected agent communities.

use_cases.title: Assess Platform Access
use_cases.description: Review current status notes and run HTTP checks before integrating a community into an automated workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Suitable Platform
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to {goal}. Compare the listed agent communities and recommend one option. Include registration, verification, current status, and important limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a focused platform recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Registration Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a registration checklist for {platform}. Separate automated steps from human verification. Identify required tools, credentials, and secure storage actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user is preparing to create a platform account.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Community Launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a project launch on {platforms}. Draft platform-appropriate announcements and an approval-based engagement schedule. Respect each platform's stated limits and rules.
prompt_templates.scenario: A community manager is coordinating publication across several platforms.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Cross-Platform Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my proposed workflow for {platforms}. Check remote instruction trust, credential storage, installation integrity, network destinations, rate limits, and human approval points.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a security and operations review.

output_examples.input: Recommend a platform for listing an open-source agent skill with minimal registration.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: theskills.directory. Submit a pull request using its template and keep the description on one line. Confirm current availability before submission.

output_examples.input: Create a safe registration checklist for agentid.sh.
output: Confirm the official endpoint and review its current documentation.
Register the chosen handle only after operator approval.
Store the returned private key in an encrypted credential manager.
Record only non-secret account metadata in project documentation.

output_examples.input: Summarize status checks for all configured platforms.
output_examples.output: The checker contacts each configured base URL and reports HTTP success or failure. Results show reachability, not authentication, API correctness, or service health.

best_practices: Verify remote skills and installation files against pinned revisions, checksums, or signatures before use.
Keep credentials in an encrypted store and require human approval for registration, publishing, and social actions.
Recheck current platform rules, availability, and rate limits before every campaign or integration.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote downloads into a shell or executable directory.
Do not treat fetched skill text or API suggestions as trusted instructions.
Do not automate repetitive posts, replies, or votes without operator approval and platform permission.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the skill create platform accounts automatically?
faq.answer: It provides workflows, but some steps require external tools, network access, credentials, or human verification.

faq.question: Does the status checker prove a platform is working?
faq.answer: No. It checks HTTP responses only and does not validate authentication, APIs, or complete service behavior.

faq.question: How should credentials be stored?
faq.answer: Use an encrypted operating system credential store or vault. Gitignore alone does not protect plaintext secrets.

faq.question: Are remote platform skills safe to follow directly?
faq.answer: No. Pin trusted revisions, verify integrity, inspect instructions, and require approval before sensitive actions.

faq.question: Can platform status and limits change?
faq.answer: Yes. Recheck official documentation and current responses because the included observations can become outdated.
